ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
Ind. Code ch. 8-1-26 provides the procedure for the Indiana Utility Regulatory 
Commission's Pipeline Safety Division ("Division") to find violations of said chapter. Upon 
review of those findings, the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
("Advisory Committee") reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case. 
The Cases received pursuant to Ind. Code ch. 8-1-26 and ripe for Commission action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations. 
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations to the 
Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Pipeline Safety 
Division and APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approved civil penalties are due within 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission. 
Any approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due. 
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, OBER, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR: 
APPROVED: 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as approved. 
Dana Kosco 
Secretary of the Commission

content.text:
2022 has the most cases, with 2,672.

| Year | Orders | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 11 | 1,603 |
| 2022 | 12 | 2,672 |
| 2023 | 14 | 2,107 |
| 2024 | 11 | 1,897 |
| 2025 | 10 | 1,684 |
| **Total** | **58** | **9,963** |

**Method:** In each order's text, page 1 is the order itself. Every later page is one recommendation form, and each of those pages contains the "finds the following violation(s)" line. I counted each order's pages after the first. I took the year from the date in each file name (for example, `ord_PSD_110321` is 11/03/2021). The order text has no printed date, so I couldn't check the file-name dates against the orders themselves.

**Nunc pro tunc order:** The `ord_PSDNPT_040622` order has one form. It corrects the damage address in Case 24633, which the Commission had already approved on 2022-02-23. I counted it as a case in 2022, because it is a recommendation form in a 2022 order. If you count only distinct case numbers, 2022 drops to 2,671. The ranking doesn't change.

**Cross-check:** Counting the "Case Number" labels gave the same totals for every order except two. Both differences come from the text extraction, not from the orders. `ord_PSD_042121` has one form whose "finds the following" line isn't machine-readable. `ord_PSD_110321` has five forms where the line is garbled or the case number is out of order. The page-based count covers all of these.
